title: Troubleshooting notes (internal) — AWS VPC Terraform modules (alpha)
content:
Purpose
- Scratchpad of issues we hit while building/testing the AWS VPC Terraform modules (alpha) + installer integration.
- Not polished. Keep adding real errors + minimal fix steps.
- Audience: Redwood Infra / PS / oncall helping pilots.


Quick triage map (start here)
1) “Installer can’t pull images / pods stuck ImagePullBackOff”
   - Almost always missing endpoints (ECR API/DKR + S3 gateway) OR private DNS disabled/broken OR security group on endpoint ENIs too tight.
   - Check VPC endpoints exist + Private DNS enabled + route tables include S3 gateway.

2) “terraform apply flakes on endpoints”
   - Eventual consistency / ordering. Re-apply works, but we added explicit depends_on in vpc-endpoints module (see PR-254).

3) “DNS weirdness / name resolves to public IP”
   - Private DNS not enabled on interface endpoints OR Route53 Resolver not reachable OR custom DHCP options forcing on-prem DNS without forwarders.

4) “STS / auth failures”
   - Missing STS interface endpoint in private-only egress environments.
   - Sometimes region mismatch (global STS vs regional STS) depending on customer policy.


Common symptoms + root causes

A) ECR image pulls fail (no public egress)
Symptoms
- Installer: “failed to pull image …”
- K8s: ImagePullBackOff
- Node logs show timeouts to api.ecr.<region>.amazonaws.com or dkr.ecr.<region>.amazonaws.com
- Sometimes: “GetAuthorizationToken” failures

Root causes
- Missing interface endpoints:
  - com.amazonaws.<region>.ecr.api
  - com.amazonaws.<region>.ecr.dkr
- Missing S3 gateway endpoint OR missing S3 route table association (ECR layers are served via S3)
- Private DNS disabled on the ECR endpoints → DNS resolves to public endpoints
- Endpoint SG too restrictive (common mistake: allow 443 from “public subnets” only; should be from workloads subnets / security groups)

Fix
- Ensure endpoints exist and are in the same VPC as the cluster/compute.
- Ensure private_dns_enabled = true (unless customer uses custom DNS approach; then they must manage split-horizon).
- Ensure S3 gateway endpoint route table associations cover private/isolated subnets used by workloads.
- Check endpoint security group:
  - inbound: 443 from the workload CIDR(s) OR from workload SG (preferred pattern)
  - outbound: generally allow all (or at least ephemeral to VPC).

Quick checks
- From a host in the private subnet:
  - dig +short api.ecr.<region>.amazonaws.com
    - Should return private IPs (VPC endpoint ENIs) not public AWS IPs.
  - curl -sS https://api.ecr.<region>.amazonaws.com (should at least TCP connect; may return 403/validation which is OK)
- AWS:
  - aws ec2 describe-vpc-endpoints --filters Name=service-name,Values=com.amazonaws.<region>.ecr.api
  - aws ec2 describe-route-tables | grep -n "pl-" (verify prefix list routes exist for S3)

Notes
- SUP-2197: pilot had ECR endpoints but missed S3 gateway endpoint association to the right route tables.


B) S3 access issues (gateway endpoint + route tables)
Symptoms
- Anything that indirectly hits S3 fails. Commonly manifests as:
  - ECR pull failures
  - Installer downloads failing
  - Timeouts to s3.<region>.amazonaws.com

Root causes
- S3 gateway endpoint created but route tables not associated (or only associated to public RT)
- Using “existing VPC adoption mode”: customer passes subnet IDs but module can’t infer their RT associations correctly unless they also pass route table IDs (we currently do NOT manage RTs in that mode; document this more clearly)

Fix
- Associate S3 gateway endpoint with route tables used by private/isolated subnets.

Quick checks
- aws ec2 describe-vpc-endpoints --vpc-endpoint-ids vpce-…
  - Confirm RouteTableIds includes the private RT(s)
- In RT, confirm a route exists to the S3 prefix list via vpce-…


C) STS/auth issues (private-only)
Symptoms
- Installer preflight: “cannot call STS” / “AccessDenied” / “Request timeout”
- Anything that needs AWS auth token retrieval fails

Root causes
- Missing interface endpoint com.amazonaws.<region>.sts
- Private DNS disabled on STS endpoint
- Customer policy forces regional STS but environment uses global endpoint (or vice versa)

Fix
- Add STS endpoint (ADR-0128 notes this as required in some topologies; we’ve seen it be effectively required for locked-down installs)
- Ensure private DNS enabled
- Align AWS SDK/CLI config to regional STS if required:
  - env var AWS_STS_REGIONAL_ENDPOINTS=regional (depends on runtime)

Quick checks
- dig +short sts.<region>.amazonaws.com
- aws sts get-caller-identity (from a host in the VPC)

Oncall note
- Slack eng-oncall thread mentioned pilot install failure tied to missing STS endpoint (workaround was temporary egress, then fixed by adding endpoint).


D) CloudWatch Logs / metrics / “logs not showing up”
Symptoms
- Flow logs configured to CloudWatch but log group empty
- Installer/agents expecting CloudWatch Logs fail to ship

Root causes
- Missing interface endpoint com.amazonaws.<region>.logs
- Endpoint policy too restrictive (if we add endpoint policies later, be careful)
- IAM role/policy missing permissions for logs:CreateLogStream / PutLogEvents

Fix
- Add logs endpoint
- Verify IAM perms for whatever is publishing

Quick checks
- dig +short logs.<region>.amazonaws.com
- aws logs describe-log-groups --log-group-name-prefix …


E) Terraform apply flakes: endpoint creation / associations
Symptoms
- terraform apply fails intermittently with errors like:
  - “Error waiting for VPC Endpoint (vpce-…) to become available: timeout”
  - “InvalidVpcEndpointId.NotFound” (immediately after create)
  - “Error creating VPC Endpoint Route Table Association: …”

Root causes
- AWS eventual consistency, esp. right after endpoint create
- Missing explicit dependencies between endpoint resources and associations / security group attachments

Fix
- Re-run apply (often works)
- Ensure using module versions including the ordering fix (PR-254)
- If still flaky: add a small sleep/backoff around associations (we avoided time_sleep but may need for some accounts/regions)

Reference
- SUP-2204: intermittent endpoint association failures; workaround was re-apply; fixed via depends_on + regression test.


F) DNS pitfalls (big bucket)
Symptoms
- Private endpoints exist, but lookups resolve to public AWS IPs
- Some names resolve, others don’t (split-horizon weirdness)
- Installer preflight says “DNS resolution failed for …”
- EKS nodes can resolve but pods cannot (or inverse)

Root causes
- Private DNS toggle off on interface endpoints
- Route53 Resolver not reachable from subnet (NACL blocks UDP/TCP 53)
- Customer uses custom DHCP options to point to on-prem DNS servers without forwarding for *.amazonaws.com zones
- Mixed resolver paths: some traffic uses VPC-provided resolver, some uses custom CoreDNS forwarding

Fix steps (in order)
1) Confirm interface endpoints have PrivateDnsEnabled = true:
   - aws ec2 describe-vpc-endpoints --vpc-endpoint-ids … | jq .VpcEndpoints[0].PrivateDnsEnabled
2) Confirm VPC DNS settings are enabled:
   - enableDnsHostnames = true
   - enableDnsSupport = true
3) Check subnet NACLs allow 53 UDP/TCP both directions within VPC.
4) If customer uses custom DNS:
   - They need conditional forwarders for:
     - *.amazonaws.com (at least the services used)
     - or specifically ecr.api/dkr, logs, sts, ssm, ec2messages, ssmmessages (if used)
   - Or they need Route53 Resolver inbound/outbound endpoints + rules.

Debug commands
- On a node/VM in the subnet:
  - cat /etc/resolv.conf
  - dig @<resolver-ip> api.ecr.<region>.amazonaws.com
  - nslookup api.ecr.<region>.amazonaws.com
  - dig +trace is not that useful inside VPC (but sometimes helps detect “not using VPC resolver”)

Random gotcha
- If endpoint private DNS is enabled, AWS creates private hosted zones behind the scenes. If customer also manually created conflicting private hosted zones, resolution can be non-deterministic.


G) “No public egress” but NAT enabled anyway
Symptoms
- Customer expects zero public traffic, but they see NAT Gateway bytes / firewall alarms

Root causes
- They left NAT mode on in tfvars
- Endpoint coverage incomplete (so workloads fallback to NAT for AWS APIs)

Fix
- For “private-only endpoints” scenario:
  - Disable NAT (or do not route 0.0.0.0/0 from private subnets to NAT)
  - Ensure endpoint set is complete for all required services
  - Installer preflight should catch missing endpoints; if it doesn’t, add checks (PR-389 improved messaging)

Notes
- This came up in Support thread: customer confusion about “private-only egress” meaning “no public internet”. We should be explicit: NAT on == potential public egress even if endpoints exist.


H) Security group baseline issues
Symptoms
- Endpoints exist, DNS resolves, but TCP connections hang/time out

Root causes
- Endpoint security group inbound rules missing from workload sources
- NACL too tight (common with enterprise templates)

Fix
- For interface endpoints:
  - inbound 443 from workload CIDRs / SGs
  - outbound ephemeral to workload
- For workload SGs:
  - ensure egress to endpoint ENI IPs/SG permitted (depending on how restrictive they are)


I) Existing VPC partial adoption mode (consume subnet IDs)
Symptoms
- terraform apply succeeds but installer preflight fails
- Endpoint created in wrong subnets or not reachable
- S3 gateway endpoint not effective

Root causes
- Subnets passed are not actually the ones used by the compute plane (customer confusion: “private” vs “isolated” naming)
- Route tables are managed outside module; S3 endpoint not associated to the right RTs
- DNS assumptions differ (shared VPC central DNS)

Fix
- Re-verify which subnet IDs are used for:
  - control plane components
  - data plane/compute
  - any jump/bastion (if used)
- If we’re not managing route tables, customer must do S3 gateway RT association themselves (doc gap)

TODO
- Add a clearer “adoption mode checklist” to quickstart + installer docs.


J) Flow logs / log delivery failures
Symptoms
- VPC Flow Logs show “REJECT” spikes unexpectedly
- Flow logs not delivered to CloudWatch/S3

Root causes
- IAM role for flow logs missing permissions
- CloudWatch log group retention/creation confusion
- For S3 destination: bucket policy missing delivery permissions

Fix
- Validate IAM role policy for flow logs
- Confirm log group exists, in same region
- If using S3: bucket policy allows delivery.logs.amazonaws.com principal (depending on AWS guidance)


Known error strings (paste from terminal; add more)
- “Error: creating EC2 VPC Endpoint (com.amazonaws.us-west-2.ecr.api): InvalidParameter: …”
- “Error: waiting for EC2 VPC Endpoint (vpce-…): timeout while waiting for state to become 'available'”
- “dial tcp: lookup api.ecr.<region>.amazonaws.com: no such host”
- “no route to host” when trying to hit S3 from isolated subnets
- “i/o timeout” from installer preflight on endpoint reachability checks


Module/dev notes
- If you see endpoint flakiness, check module version includes:
  - explicit depends_on between endpoint + associations
  - any provider retry tuning
- If something looks like a provider bug, capture:
  - terraform version
  - aws provider version
  - region
  - exact error and resource address
  - whether re-apply succeeds


Installer preflight alignment (what it should catch)
- DNS resolution for:
  - api.ecr.<region>.amazonaws.com
  - dkr.ecr.<region>.amazonaws.com
  - sts.<region>.amazonaws.com
  - logs.<region>.amazonaws.com
- Basic HTTPS connect to those endpoints
- S3 connectivity (ideally via a simple signed request; currently we do a simpler reachability check)

If preflight error is not actionable
- File ticket against installer with:
  - preflight output
  - tfvars used
  - list of endpoints created
  - dig output from inside VPC


Open questions / TODOs
- Decide if STS endpoint should be “required” in our alpha docs or “required for private-only/no-NAT topologies”. Evidence says: treat as required for the locked-down template.
- Existing VPC mode: do we need optional inputs for route table IDs to manage S3 gateway association safely?
- Consider adding explicit checks to terraform (validation blocks) for contradictory settings:
  - private_dns_enabled=false + no NAT + expecting private-only install => will break


Changelog
- 2024-11-29: initial notes collected during module bring-up
- 2025-01-10: added endpoint flake section + SUP-2204 reference
- 2025-02-22: added STS endpoint notes + adoption-mode pitfalls based on pilot feedback
